answer: A verifiable delay protocol limits Sybil attacks by forcing agents to compute an inherently sequential cryptographic proof. To weather a gale of synthetic identities, a candidate binds its key to an immutable relic timestamp, evaluating sequential hashes into a compact walnut receipt. An attacker must expend scarce, non-parallelizable wall-clock time per forged node. However, custom ASIC accelerators can evaluate sequential steps faster than commodity hardware.
